caption: Label data audit: (a) class distribution, (b) UACR per class, (c) urine albumin–creatinine space with iso-UACR lines at 30 and 300 mg/g, (d) age distribution.
Characteristics of the unified dataset: (a) repeats per sample, (b) illumination per class, (c) number of tests per class.
Visual verification of ROI detection on example albumin–creatinine image pairs from each class: original image, ROI mask contour, and the final ROI used for quantification.
Feature extraction summary: (a) feature composition, (b) distribution of ROI area, (c) proportion of specular pixels.
Distribution of key colorimetric features (mean G, CIELAB b*, ΔE to white, saturation) in the albumin (top) and creatinine (bottom) images by class.
Hierarchically clustered Spearman correlation map between key albumin (alb__) and creatinine (cre__) features; red blocks indicate redundant features.
PCA projection of all features: (a) by class, (b) by lux, (c) explained variance. Class silhouette on the first 5 PCs = 0.029.
Construct validity: (top) the 12 features with the highest Spearman correlation to laboratory values; (bottom) scatter plots of the best feature. Descriptive sample-level analysis (mean of repeats).

Feature sensitivity to illumination (lux): (a) distribution of |ρ| over all features, (b) the 12 most sensitive features. Lux-sensitive features risk carrying acquisition variation rather than chemical information.
Data cleansing: (a) distribution of feature ICC and the reliability threshold, (b) ICC by method group and image source, (c) multivariate outliers in PCA space.
Intra-sample coefficient of variation of feature alb__G_mean across repeats, by class; overall median = 2.03%.
Fold plan: (a) class composition of the outer test folds (repeat 1); (b) distribution of the number of repeats per sample, which is why splits are made by sample.
